factorRatings.note: The Infatuation (7.8/10) praises this Delridge takeout window's naturally leavened, long-fermented pies for charred, bubbled crusts and bold tang, calling it a fix for a Neapolitan-shaped hole in West Seattle, while noting not every topping combo lands.

The Infatuation scores this Interbay pop-up 8.4/10, calling its confit-garlic pepperoni pie flawless and its crust sturdy with sourdough-like chew, crisp bottom and charred, crackly bubbles; it operates out of Batch 206 Distillery.

A Chinatown-ID fixture since opening in Belltown in 1992 (relocated to King St in 2011), World Pizza is one of the city's few vegetarian-only slice shops, cited by Thrillist and Seattle Metropolitan for inventive toppings like gorgonzola-potato-rosemary on an unfussy, utilitarian crust.

Seattle Times critic Providence Cicero gave Pulcinella three stars for VPN-certified true Neapolitan pizza baked in about 90 seconds in an imported Valoriani wood oven; The Infatuation still sends readers to Rainier Beach for a margherita well above heat-lamp-slice territory.
